findings.anchor: .claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:Mode: heuristic unless the operator opts in through .loa.config.yaml
findings.description: The new authoritative-mode opt-in is read from `$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml`, but that file is inside the project workspace and is not protected by this hook because it is outside the App Zone. A model/session can first write `.loa.config.yaml` with `implement_gate.mode: authoritative`, then send a model-authored `tool_input.active_skill` such as `implement` and silently allow subsequent `src/`, `lib/`, or `app/` writes. This violates the stated invariant that only an operator opt-in selects authoritative mode and that model-authored `tool_input` must not select or bypass the gate.
findings.failure_mode: A forged two-step write bypasses the App Zone compliance ask: write project config to enable authoritative mode, then perform an App Zone Write/Edit with forged `tool_input.active_skill=implement`; the hook exits 0 without `decision: ask`.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not trust repo-local `.loa.config.yaml` for this security decision. Move the opt-in to an operator-controlled location outside the project writable surface, require an environment variable set by the harness/operator, or make writes to `.loa.config.yaml` that affect `implement_gate.mode` fail-ask/protected before the mode can change.

findings.description: The change moves the authoritative-mode trust anchor from .run/platform-features.json to $PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml on the stated grounds that tool_input is model-authored and so nothing the model can write may select the mode. But .loa.config.yaml is also a plain file inside the project that the model writes with the same Write/Edit tools, and this very hook classifies it as non-App-Zone and exits 0 silently (zone check: only src/, lib/, app/ are gated). A model can therefore (1) Write .loa.config.yaml with `implement_gate:\n  mode: authoritative`, then (2) Write src/x.ts with tool_input.active_skill: "implement" and receive a silent allow with no ask and no audit line. IG-5 ("whatever .run/ claims") and IG-11 (key stays undocumented) pin a property that only holds if some other hook protects .loa.config.yaml; the hook source itself is readable to the model, so the undocumented key is not a control. The old code also logged compliance.mode.change to audit.jsonl; the new selection path writes nothing, so an authoritative session leaves no trace of why App Zone writes were allowed.
findings.failure_mode: If no separate hook guards .loa.config.yaml writes, the operator-only opt-in is self-grantable by the model in two tool calls, and every subsequent App Zone write with a forged active_skill bypasses the FAIL-ASK gate silently and unlogged.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) have this hook treat writes to $PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml (and .loa.config.yaml.* ) as gated, emitting {"decision":"ask"} regardless of zone, or confirm an existing protected-files hook covers it and reference it in the header comment; (b) read the opt-in from a location the model cannot author via tool_input (operator shell env var or ~/.config/loa/), falling back to the repo file only for display; and (c) restore an audit.jsonl event (e.g. compliance.mode.selected with source: .loa.config.yaml) whenever compliance_mode becomes authoritative, so an allowed write is attributable.

findings.description: Mode selection requires `command -v yq` and runs `yq '.implement_gate.mode // ""' file`. If yq is absent, or is Go yq v3 (which uses `yq r FILE PATH` syntax and errors on this expression), or is the Python jq-wrapper yq with a YAML the wrapper rejects, the error is swallowed by `2>/dev/null || configured_mode=""` and the operator's explicit opt-in is silently ignored. Nothing is written to audit.jsonl or stderr. The hook also calls yq on every App Zone write rather than once, so the silent failure repeats indefinitely. The quote-stripping `${configured_mode//\"/}` papers over the Python-vs-Go output difference but not the v3 syntax difference.
findings.failure_mode: An operator who sets implement_gate.mode: authoritative on a machine with yq v3 or no yq gets heuristic behaviour with no indication; because the fallback direction is toward asking, the symptom is spurious ADVISORY prompts that look like a hook bug rather than a missing dependency.
findings.suggested_fix: When .loa.config.yaml exists and contains the implement_gate key (cheap grep) but yq is missing or exits non-zero, append a one-line compliance.config.unreadable event to $RUN_DIR/audit.jsonl (guarded by the same once-only pattern used by the evidence recorder) and/or emit a single stderr note. Prefer the repository's existing config-reading helper if one exists so yq-flavour handling lives in one place.

findings.cross_file_justification: The new evidence recorder in implement-gate.sh creates or rewrites .run/platform-features.json via mktemp+mv, which refreshes the file's mtime. detect-platform-features.sh owns that file and, per the new test IG-9 (which must `touch -d '2 hours ago'` before invoking it), uses an mtime-based freshness cache.
findings.description: When no platform-features.json exists yet, the recorder writes a three-key object ({active_skill_available:false, active_skill_seen_at, active_skill_source}) with a brand-new mtime. If detect-platform-features.sh treats a file younger than its cache window as authoritative and returns it without re-detecting, every other feature field it normally populates (detected_at, schema_version, harness_signal, any further platform flags) is absent for the rest of the window, and any consumer reading those fields sees null. The same applies when the recorder rewrites an existing file: its mtime is bumped, extending the cache lifetime of possibly stale detections by up to the full window.
findings.failure_mode: For up to the cache window after the first lead-session payload carrying active_skill, `/loa` status and any other reader of platform-features.json may operate on a sparse or stale detection record because the file looks freshly detected.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the recorder preserve the original mtime (e.g. `touch -r "$FEATURES_FILE" "$_ig_tmp"` before mv when the file existed), or have detect-platform-features.sh key its cache on `.detected_at` rather than mtime and treat a file lacking detected_at as a cache miss. Add a bats case: recorder runs on an absent file, then detect runs within the window and still performs detection.

findings.description: CH-T8, CH-T9, IG-7, IG-8 and the opt-in half of IG-10 all `skip "yq not installed"`. The implementation report claims CH-T8 "no longer passes vacuously", but on any CI image without yq the entire authoritative branch of implement-gate.sh (the only branch that can produce a silent allow on a forged payload) runs zero assertions and the suite is green. The gate code itself also degrades silently without yq (DISS-002), so a missing yq hides both the behaviour and its tests at once.
findings.failure_mode: A regression in the authoritative branch (e.g. a widened case pattern or a dropped fallback) ships undetected on CI runners that lack yq, while local runs with yq pass; the report's non-vacuity claim does not hold in that environment.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare yq as a required test dependency and fail rather than skip when running under CI (e.g. `[[ -n "${CI:-}" ]] && fail "yq required" || skip`), or vendor a minimal yq-free parser path for the single scalar key so the branch is testable everywhere and the skip can be removed.
